subject: Re: Redwood Private — VPC / air-gapped feasibility & next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Redwood Private — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Jane / Acme team,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of ask (from your side)
- You need an inference deployment option that can run inside Acme VPC with no outbound egress from the model hosts (air-gap-friendly).
- Control plane connectivity is acceptable if it can be tunneled over S2S VPN or proxy and restricted to a handful of IPs.
- Must support customer-managed KMS (HSM) for key wrapping and audit logs for model inputs/outputs retention policy (90 days).
- Evaluation to include performance comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoints and a TCO sketch.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Redwood Private (VPC): customer-managed control plane with optional egressless model nodes (control plane can be isolated).
- Air-gap feasibility: we support an on-prem, air-gapped deploy path — image bundles + offline installer for approved environments.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration, audit log streams to your SIEM, SOC2 evidence library.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers: unified serving runtime optimized for low-latency inference, intelligent batching, and model-variant fallback to improve reliability during capacity constraints.

Proposed next steps
1) Marcus to share a short network diagram and a checklist of control-plane/network requirements. (Marcus: can you attach?)
2) Acme to confirm whether outbound only to control-plane IPs over S2S VPN is acceptable, or if the model hosts must have zero outbound.
3) If acceptable, we run a 1-week in-VPC performance test (benchmarking latency & throughput) and a short functional eval in an air-gapped lab.
4) Procurement to request SOW + initial timeline.

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-nw-diagram.pdf (high-level network flow)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus and Lauren into technical follow-ups.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Jane — thanks for the clarifications. Looping Marcus (Solutions) and Lauren (Security) to address the two main threads: networking/control-plane behavior and air-gap/upgrade process. 

Quick notes while Marcus crafts the diagram: 
- Control plane: we support two modes for Private deployments: 
  1) Managed control plane (Redwood-hosted, requires outbound to a limited set of IPs)
  2) Customer-hosted control plane (recommended for strict no-egress — control plane lives in your account or on-prem)

- Data plane: can be configured to disallow any outbound egress. All inference requests and KV cache stay inside your VPC; model telemetry is optional and can be disabled.

- Upgrades / telemetry: for air-gapped installs we provide signed image bundles and an offline installer. For customer-hosted control plane we provide upgrade artifacts and a checklist; the upgrade process does not phone home unless you opt-in for managed updates.

Marcus / Lauren — can you confirm the specific ports/protocols and provide a slightly expanded diagram so Acme's network team can review? Also attaching our standard SOW draft (SOW-draft-Redwood-Acme-v1.docx) to help Procurement start.

Thanks,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Redwood Private — network checklist and suggested tests

Hi Jane — following up with the technical checklist and suggested validation steps. Attached a slightly expanded diagram.

Key network/control-plane items (customer-hosted control plane recommended for strict no-egress):
- Required inbound/outbound: 
  - Control plane management port: TCP 443 (outbound from admin jump host to control-plane endpoint) if using managed control plane.
  - For customer-hosted control plane: control-plane services run on customer subnet; only admin jump to control-plane over S2S VPN needed.
  - Model hosts (data plane): no outbound routes recommended; NACLs/security groups should prevent 0.0.0.0/0 egress.

Air-gap and installer flow:
- We provide a signed tarball with container images + a checksum and instructions. Image push can be done via an internal registry (Harbor / ECR) — we can provide a script to import images into your registry.
- Upgrades: offline artifact + runbook. Operators run the upgrade from inside the VPC; no outbound required.

KMS/HSM integration:
- We support AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and CloudHSM integrations. For HSM-backed wrapping keys, we only require network access from the control plane to the KMS endpoint (can be private endpoints).

Suggested short tests for POC (1 week):
1) Import images to your sandbox VPC and stand up model nodes with egress disabled. Verify model starts and healthchecks succeed.
2) Run latency/throughput benchmark against your baseline hyperscaler endpoint (we'll provide a small harness).
3) Validate KMS calls via private endpoint and confirm audit log export.
4) Test a failover where control plane is unreachable but model nodes continue serving cached KV prefix for a short window — verify behavior.

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-nw-diagram.pdf (expanded)

I'll be available for a technical call with your network/security folks — propose Thu 10am PT if that works.

Cheers,
Marcus

Hi Jane — quick security notes for Acme's reviewers: 

- Telemetry & data: telemetry is optional; we will ship with telemetry off by default for air-gapped installs. Model input/output logging is configurable with retention policy (we can set to 90 days and stream to your SIEM).
- Evidence: we can provide our SOC2 report, pen test summary, and an audit log mapping doc. I'll share redacted artifacts under an NDA; for customer-hosted control plane we also provide a runbook for key rotation and HSM integration.
- Risk/controls: offline installer signatures, image checksums, and RBAC scoped to admin jump hosts.

If your security team prefers, we can do a short 45-minute walkthrough of the SOW and deliverables and then share the artifacts behind an NDA.

Hi — thanks for the ask. Attaching SOW draft (SOW-draft-Redwood-Acme-v1.docx). High-level answers below so your team can move quickly: 

POC: 1-week sandbox run — target start within 1 week of image & network access (we estimate 2-3 business days to prepare artifacts once NDA + sandbox access provided).
POC pricing: typically covered as a free evaluation for strategic deals — if procurement prefers a billable POC we can provide a one-off line item; I'll confirm in the attached SOW.
12-month Dedicated deployment: pricing bands included in SOW (small/medium/large GPU pools). Minimum commit: typically monthly reserved GPU hours for Dedicated; details in SOW.
OS/patching for customer-hosted control plane: customer owns host OS patching and container registry; Redwood supports runtime component patches delivered as container images. We provide the runbook and automation scripts to make upgrades straightforward.

Next steps: I'll schedule the technical call between Marcus+Lauren and your security/network team for Thu 10am PT unless you propose otherwise. Will also send the NDA + SOC2 artifacts link to Jane.
